mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a financial crisis.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced consumer demand for goods and services, which negatively impacts corporate revenues and thus S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of offsetting fiscal stimulus.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, reducing wage growth and consumer spending, which in turn depresses corporate earnings and S&P 500 returns over the following 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is reversed during periods of aggressive monetary easing.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and lowers profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from baseline during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual monetary-inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and increases uncertainty, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong global demand.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 500k units signals a collapse in residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and drags down S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 500k in a single month after > 600k the prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered episodes compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a two-month period indicates labor market churning, often preceding a recession, and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE increases over two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not robust during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 5-year average signals reduced household buffer capacity, which increases sensitivity to income shocks and reduces consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered episodes compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.10).
